outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Overview of Parameter-Efficient Finetuning
outline.description: Introduces the need for efficient adaptation of large foundation models and situates BOFT within the broader PEFT landscape. Presents the core idea: using orthogonal transformations for finetuning and improving their parameter efficiency via butterfly factorization.
subtopics: Why finetuning foundation models matters: cost and scalability
PEFT categories: model finetuning, adapters, prompts
Limitations of ad hoc small learning rates and unstructured updates
Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) as a principled approach: preserve neuron geometry
The core challenge: orthogonal matrices are high-dimensional
High-level idea of BOFT: compose dense orthogonal transforms from sparse, structured factors

outline.description: Reviews linear algebra and optimization tools underpinning OFT and BOFT, focusing on orthogonality, parameterizations, and stability properties relevant to finetuning.
subtopics: Orthogonal matrices: definitions, properties, and orthogonal groups
Angle preservation and why it preserves relational neuron information
Skew-symmetric matrices and Cayley transform: R = (I + Q)(I − Q)^{-1}
SVD and spectral norm; why left-multiplying by orthogonal matrices preserves spectral norm
Block-diagonal structures: parameter counts and inductive biases
Low-rank additive reparameterization (LoRA) vs multiplicative orthogonal updates

outline.chapter_title: Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): Design, Benefits, and Limitations
outline.description: Explains OFT in detail: how it transforms pretrained weights, how orthogonality is maintained during learning, and why block-diagonal OFT trades expressivity for parameter savings.
subtopics: OFT forward pass: z = (R W0)^T x with layer-shared R
Cayley parameterization in practice for maintaining orthogonality
Identity initialization and preserving the pretrained model at start
Block-diagonal OFT: structure, parameter counts, and training stability
Expressivity limits of block-diagonal orthogonals (fixed sparsity pattern)
Comparison to LoRA: multiplicative vs additive, geometry vs rank constraints
Empirical strengths of OFT and its parameter footprint

outline.chapter_title: A Graphical Information Transmission Framework for Matrix Factorization
outline.description: Recasts orthogonal matrix construction as an information transmission problem on a layered grid graph, clarifying how sparse factors compose dense connectivity and where parameter savings arise.
subtopics: Matrix-as-graph view: nonzero entries as edges enabling information flow
Factorization as multi-layer transmission: d × (m+1) grid interpretation
Desiderata: dense connectivity with minimal free edges
Orthogonality constraints: bijective connections and per-layer d edges
Parameter efficiency vs edge count; why single dense matrices cost O(d^2)
Illustrative examples contrasting feasible vs infeasible sparsity patterns
Why block-diagonal OFT cannot realize dense connectivity

outline.chapter_title: Butterfly Structures: From FFT to Sparse Factorizations
outline.description: Introduces butterfly graphs from the Cooley–Tukey FFT, and shows how their structure leads to sparse, composable matrices that transmit information efficiently.
subtopics: Cooley–Tukey algorithm and the butterfly communication pattern
Butterfly factor B^F(k): 2×2 block with diagonal subblocks
Butterfly components ẐB(d, k) and recursive construction of B(d)
Block butterfly extension: replacing scalars with b×b blocks
Permutation structure and equivalence among components
Complexity: O(d log d) nonzeros vs O(d^2) for dense matrices
Ability to realize classic fast transforms (FFT, DCT, Hadamard)

outline.chapter_title: Orthogonal Butterfly Finetuning (BOFT): Method and Implementation
outline.description: Presents BOFT: composing an orthogonal matrix as a product of orthogonal butterfly components to achieve dense transforms with O(d log d) parameters.
subtopics: BOFT definition: R(m, b) = ∏_{i=1}^m ẐB^b_{(d,i)} with each component orthogonal
Special cases: BOFT(1, b) = block-diagonal OFT; BOFT(1, d) = full OFT
Dense orthogonals via butterfly: m = log d, b = 2
Parameter count: 0.5(b − 1) d m; dense with any b in BOFT
Identity initialization for stable start
Multiplicative Dropout: randomly replacing selected components/blocks with identity (p1, p2)
Training/inference: composing during training, folding into W0 post-training for zero latency
Practical choices of where to apply R in a layer (left-multiplication on input dimension)

outline.chapter_title: Theoretical Insights: Expressivity, Stability, and Inductive Bias
outline.description: Analyzes BOFT’s hypothesis class, approximation ability, stability, and implicit biases induced by the butterfly structure.
subtopics: Expressivity improvement over block-diagonal OFT at fixed block size
Kaleidoscope hierarchy: alternating butterfly products to span the orthogonal group
Expressivity–regularity trade-off: why smaller classes can generalize better
Spectral norm preservation and implications for stability
Bilinear similarity interpretation: learning w_i^0 R x under orthogonality
Weight interpolation across factorized components and training dynamics
Inductive bias from fast-transform structures and sparse factorization

outline.description: Guides practical deployment in Transformers, vision, and diffusion models, covering dimensioning, numerics, and efficiency.
subtopics: Where to apply BOFT in Transformers: attention projections (Q,K,V,O) and MLPs
Handling non-power-of-two dimensions: padding, mixed radix, permutations
Choosing m and b under a parameter budget; per-layer allocation strategies
Cayley parameterization numerics: forming Q, ensuring (I − Q) invertibility
Mixed-precision and stability considerations
Multiplicative Dropout hyperparameters and schedules
Computational overhead during training vs no overhead at inference
Integration with other PEFT methods and quantization pipelines

outline.description: Summarizes experimental evidence that BOFT outperforms strong PEFT baselines while using fewer parameters across LLMs, ViTs, and diffusion models.
subtopics: Benchmarks: language understanding/generation, vision classification/transfer, text-to-image
Baselines: full finetuning, LoRA variants, OFT (block/full), adapters, prompts
Parameter efficiency vs performance curves; stability under small data
Ablations: varying m and b, component permutations, Dropout usage
Training stability and spectral behavior comparisons
Case studies and qualitative analyses (e.g., controllable generation)
Compute/time trade-offs and practical throughput

outline.chapter_title: Relationships to Other PEFT and Butterfly-Based Methods
outline.description: Clarifies how BOFT differs from low-rank and butterfly-parameterized training from scratch, and when to prefer hybrids.
subtopics: BOFT vs LoRA: multiplicative orthogonal vs additive low-rank updates
BOFT vs OFT: subsuming block/full OFT and providing dense transforms at lower cost
Butterfly-based reparameterization in prior work: training from scratch vs finetuning
Projection-based butterfly finetuning vs layer-shared orthogonal transformation
Hybrid approaches: low-rank plus butterfly, adapter-plus-BOFT combinations
Inference latency considerations across methods

outline.chapter_title: Limitations, Practical Pitfalls, and Future Directions
outline.description: Discusses known limitations, open questions, and promising research directions inspired by the information transmission view.
subtopics: Training-time overhead from multiple factors; kernel-level optimizations
Topology optimality: are there denser or better sparse factorization graphs?
Automated selection of m, b, and permutations per layer/task
Approximation guarantees and tighter expressivity bounds
Beyond orthogonality: near-orthogonal or unitary variants, complex-valued transforms
Robustness, safety, and evaluation under distribution shift
Drawing from computer networking for novel information transmission topologies

outline.chapter_title: Summary, Study Questions, and Project Ideas
outline.description: Recaps key concepts and provides guided exercises and project suggestions to cement understanding and encourage exploration.
subtopics: Key takeaways: information transmission perspective and butterfly factorization
Concept checks: Cayley transform, parameter counts, dense connectivity criteria
Derivation exercises: build BOFT for a toy layer and verify orthogonality
Implementation lab: add BOFT to a Transformer block and fold weights post-training
Ablation study design: explore m, b, and Dropout on a small benchmark
Research projects: new sparse topologies; hybrid PEFTs; layer-wise topology search
